messages:
ashley: quick RFC follow-up — re: service auth surface. after the design review i sketched two smaller steps to reduce blast radius. TL;DR: (1) narrow api-key runtime semantics, (2) add short-lived delegation tokens for cross-project calls.
priya: +1 on incremental. can you sketch the runtime rules again? i worry about existing long-lived keys in customer integrations.
mike: also curious how this interacts with Dedicated/Dedicated-private routing — we can't require every infra path to mint ephemeral tokens.
ashley: yeah that's the tradeoff. suggestion: keep the existing long-lived api keys for ingress (create/run), but ban them from being propagated across project boundaries. for cross-project calls we require a short-lived delegated token stamped with origin-project and allowed-intents.
jordan: how short-lived? 5m? 1h? what's the practical window for background jobs?
ashley: proposal: two types — "interactive" delegations (5m) for user-facing calls and "worker" delegations (1h) that require explicit workload registration + scoped rate limits. both are minted by the auth proxy and audited.
priya: sounds reasonable. what's the mint API like? inline example pls.
ashley: sure — pseudo: ```POST /v1/delegate
{ "from_key":"api_XXXX","target_project":"proj-abc","intents":["embed:create","model:invoke"],"ttl":300 }
``` returns a JWT-like token with claims: sub, from_project, allowed_intents, exp, sig.
mike: JWT means we need key rotation and verification libs everywhere. do we want opaque tokens instead?
ashley: opaque tokens are easier for rotation but harder for offline verification in Dedicated/private where we don't want a central call. we can make tokens self-verifiable (short TTL) + allow an optional introspect endpoint for older flows.
jordan: what about RBAC mapping? if a token has allowed_intents, do we still check role bindings at service endpoint? duplicate checks = extra latency.
priya: i'd prefer defence-in-depth. token should be coarse allowlist, and endpoints enforce fine-grained RBAC. but we can optimize common hot-paths by embedding role-assertions in the token for pre-authorized flows.
mike: embedding role assertions makes tokens larger and harder to rotate privileges. plus it couples authz rules into token minting.
ashley: agreed — to balance: tokens carry minimal intent and subject; we keep per-route feature flags that can accept token-asserted roles for performance-critical routes, with a documented opt-in.
ashley: operationally: auth-proxy will log: mint request, auditable mapping: who requested, source key fingerprint, resulting delegated token id (not the secret). infra-bot: deploy note -> we will emit a trace id on every mint for correlation. :gear: 
priya: migration path for existing keys? we should provide an opt-in shim: proxy can mint worker delegations automatically for calls that would cross projects while we phase out propagation.
mike: ok. fallback behavior: if delegation fails, should we 403 or allow fallback to legacy propagation? i vote 403 for safety but with a clear errors page + migration tooling.
jordan: 403 for safety makes sense. we should surface a specific error code so customers can detect and auto-instrument retries to mint.
ashley: yes — error code AUTH_DELEGATION_REQUIRED with a link to a one-click migration checklist.
priya: any perf concerns? extra hop to mint per cross-project call could add latency. can we cache delegated tokens per caller-target-intent for short windows?
ashley: caching allowed, proxy owns TTL semantics. recommend caching at most 30s for interactive flows, 10m for worker flows. limit cache size per origin to avoid explosion.
mike: note: Dedicated/private customers may want to disable remote mint and host a local delegation service. design should allow a pluggable mint backend.
ashley: agreed — design will include an interface: local_mint_backend vs hosted_mint. private mode defaults to local.
priya: docs TODO: a migration runbook, errors mapping, sample code for mint + verify, and a rollout plan (canary + blackout window).
jordan: i'll volunteer to own the rollout checklist. mike can you scope the SDK changes for token verification?
mike: yeah i'll put up a small RFC for SDK surface: TokenVerifier.verify(token) -> {valid, claims}. also add helper mint convenience in server-side SDKs.
ashley: great. next steps: i'll open a short RFC PR with the API contract + opt-in rollout schedule. pls comment on the TTL numbers and cache defaults. thanks all. :sparkles:
